title: Brave Love Premiere and Behind the Scenes of the New Telenovela
seoTitle: Brave Love Premiere: Behind the Scenes of SBT Telenovela
subtitle: The Mexican production starring Silvia Navarro and Cristián de la Fuente arrives in prime time with government backing and animal care
excerpt: The Mexican telenovela Brave Love premiered in SBT's prime time slot, scoring solid ratings in Greater São Paulo while behind-the-scenes details were revealed.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The Mexican telenovela Brave Love has premiered on SBT, instantly driving audience search trends and shaking up the prime-time schedule. Starring Silvia Navarro and Cristián de la Fuente, the plot arrives in Brazil following a history of international broadcasts and a production process that involved state support and special security protocols.

How the Premiere and Television Ratings Played Out

The first episode of the Mexican telenovela scored an average of 3.8 points in Greater São Paulo, securing third place for the network. The show replaces The Story of Joan, the Virgin, initially airing in a double-feature format during its predecessor's final weeks. This performance maintains the audience share recorded by other recent foreign productions on the channel.

Government Support and Filming in Mexico

The production relied on the support of the State of Mexico government to facilitate part of the filming in municipalities such as Aculco and Metepec. The collaboration aimed to promote the region's landscapes, architecture, and tourist attractions. The governor at the time participated in the launch alongside the cast and production crew.

Care for Bulls and Casting Choices

The rural universe is central to the story, as the character Camila works as a veterinarian on a fighting bull ranch. The presence of the animals required hiring specialists and utilizing local farm workers for the most dangerous scenes. The production emphasized that the work's primary focus is the love story and the portrayal of livestock farming, rather than bullfighting.

International Performance and Arrival in Brazil

In Mexico, the show finished sixth among the country's most-watched fiction series in its production year. In the United States, the results were even more impressive on Univision, ranking among the most-watched productions on US Hispanic television. Now, the story lands in Brazil as SBT's new bet for its audience.

With information from Terra, Observatório da TV, NaTelinha.
